source.title: In-Context Learning Beyond Copying: A Training-Time Analysis of Abstractive ICL
source.authors: Kerem Şahin; Sheridan Feucht; Adam Belfki; Jannik Brinkmann; Aaron Mueller; David Bau; C. Wendler

page_placements.theme: Induction-like attention from random or frozen query-key weights

record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on training to reduce induction-predictable copying and reports that abstractive ICL can still emerge without the canonical induction-head transition, refining the proposed link between induction circuits and ICL.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on copying, induction-head measurements, abstractive ICL, token-loss difference, and head interventions. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. Values presented only in figures are identified as figure-only.
record.test_reason: The authors train 1B and 2.8B GPT-NeoX models on the Pile with the loss masked at induction-predictable positions (HAPAX). They measure induction-head formation, copying, token-loss difference (TLD) and abstractive few-shot ICL. These results bear directly on V2, V3, V5 and V6, and weakly on V4. They argue that V3 overstates the link between induction heads and ICL.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that HAPAX models develop fewer and weaker induction heads. They conclude that the developmental link between induction-circuit phenomena and abstractive ICL is weaker than previously hypothesized, and that the phase transition is tied to repeated, induction-predictable structure in the data.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT-NeoX-based models from scratch with loss masking at induction-predictable positions, rather than reproducing the original induction-head measurement and training setup. It also uses a similarity-thresholded masking variant and evaluates abstractive few-shot tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Masking strength changes outcomes: exact-match H APAX and similarity-thresholded H APAX differ in copying and abstractive task performance. Standard versus target-excluded evaluation also changes comparisons. The random-masked baseline was run only for the first 5000 steps.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 1B full transformer, the top prefix-matching heads promote the copied token less often under HAPAX, and many suppress it (anti-induction-like). Patching previous-token-head output into a random-initialization model raises prefix matching from 0.076 to 0.122.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In large transformers, prefix-matching attention can partly reflect initialization-level tendencies plus previous-token information, and can come apart from copying output.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The main 1B training comparisons use a single random seed per condition. Supplemental seeds differ in precision and GPU ecosystem. The study's conclusions concern selected few-shot abstractive tasks and training conditions; the Random-Masked baseline was limited to 5000 steps. Some training-trajectory results are shown in figures without numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports further task-level accuracies in Tables A2-A7 and H11-H13, additional head-ablation and concept-head analyses in Figures A2-A17, and auxiliary training variants in Appendix E. These are not separately extracted because the aggregate task summaries and directly relevant head measurements are retained, and the additional task-by-task values would exceed the useful scope of this record.

untested.parts: No small attention-only transformers are studied. The mechanism analyses (logit lens, patching) are on 1B full transformers.
Loss-curve bump timing is not quantified numerically. The ICL coincidence is tested only through TLD and abstractive tasks.
Models above 2.8B, and ICL forms beyond the 34 abstractive few-shot tasks and TLD, are not tested.
Other model families, architectures and modalities are not tested. Only GPT-NeoX/Pile at 1B and 2.8B, plus two extra seeds.
Only the loss-masking interventions are tested. Other data properties (for example burstiness or Zipfian skew) are not.
Whether formation splits into sub-steps is not analysed.

missing.what: Random-Masked baseline at step 5000: repetition accuracy 93.5% versus 93.7% for Vanilla and 13.3% for HAPAX; validation loss 2.70 versus 2.67 and 3.76. This is the control showing that the position choice, not the amount masked, suppresses copying.
Extra seeds 1337 and 2807: Vanilla has 8 and 9 of 128 heads above 80%, while HAPAX has 1 and 2. Vanilla TLD peaks at 0.45 at step 1600; abstractive ICL stays below 3% until step 3000 in both models.
2.8B prefix-matching trajectories (Figure H43), repetition accuracy (Figure H41) and TLD (Figure H44) for Vanilla versus HAPAX
Ablating the top 2 previous-token heads drives Vanilla abstractive accuracy near 0; the effect is smaller in the HAPAX variants
Extractive ICL task accuracies drop under HAPAX on all but one significant task

record.verdict_notes: V1 is not tested: these are 1B and 2.8B full transformers, so the mechanism rows were unlinked. R11 and R12 were re-stated as observed for V3 and V5, because a TLD loss after removing induction signal is what those versions predict. Rows R14-R22 are linked to both V3 and V6; their state is phrased for V6 and is the opposite for V3. The main runs use a single seed, and the Thresholded variant confounds less copying with less supervision. The text says non-extractive TLD in HAPAX is both higher than and statistically indifferent to Vanilla.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly establish the full causal composition of a trained induction head with an earlier previous-token head; its patching experiment measures prefix-matching after adding previous-token information.
The study tests its training conditions and measured loss/ICL metrics, not all models or training setups.
The study evaluates selected few-shot abstractive tasks at 1B and 2.8B, not most forms of ICL or larger-scale models generally.
Tests are within GPT-NeoX-based models and Pile training; other model families, architectures, modalities, and broad size ranges are not tested.
The tested training/data changes are the reported exact-match and similarity-thresholded loss masking regimes; other data properties and training setups are not tested.
The study analyzes function-vector heads and selected previous-token-head ablations, not every mechanism or kind of few-shot task learning.
The study does not test whether vanilla induction-head formation consists of multiple distinct sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Vanilla
rows.operation_detail: Counted heads attaining a prefix-matching score above 80% during training.
rows.measure: Number of heads with prefix-matching score above 80%
rows.note: The paper describes the Vanilla heads as peaking suddenly early in training and then decaying.
rows.check: In the Vanilla model, 12 of 128 heads exceed 80% prefix matching; they peak suddenly early in training and then decay. This bears on V2 (abrupt and early) and V4 (presence). V1 was removed: these are 1B full transformers, not small attention-only ones.

rows.subject: H APAX
rows.operation_detail: Trained with loss contributions masked at induction-predictable positions, then measured prefix matching.
rows.measure: Number of heads with prefix-matching score above 80%
rows.note: The remaining prefix-matching development is described as unfolding gradually over 1800 steps, rather than showing the Vanilla transition.
rows.check: Under masking, only 1 head exceeds 80%, and it emerges gradually over about 1800 steps. For V5 (formation depends on training) this is observed, not partial. V1 and V4 removed.

rows.check: The text groups the two HAPAX variants. The Figure 6 caption says only 1 head ever exceeds 80% in HAPAX, so the separate Thresholded count is not clearly stated. No transition is shown. V1 and V4 removed.

rows.subject: Randomly initialized Vanilla model
rows.stage_stated: random initialization, with layer-L4 activation patched from step 5000
rows.operation_detail: Patched layer-L4 output from the step-5000 Vanilla model into the randomly initialized model.
rows.note: The paper says two of the top three final H APAX prefix-matching heads also increase their scores in this patching experiment.
rows.check: Patching previous-token output into a random-initialization 1B model raises maximum prefix matching from 0.076 to 0.122. This is a composition-related finding in a different system from V1, and it is about initialization rather than trained heads.

rows.subject: Vanilla
rows.operation_detail: Measured token-loss difference (loss at position 50 minus loss at position 500) on all validation samples.
rows.value: The metric shows a sudden improvement during training.
rows.note: The authors interpret this all-sample metric as primarily reflecting inductive copying.
rows.check: The Vanilla all-sample TLD shows a sudden improvement. The authors attribute it mainly to inductive copying, which fits V3's loss-by-token-index definition.
